structure.overview: This case concerns Pfizer's patent impeachment action against uniQure's patent related to a modified Factor IX protein used in gene therapy for hemophilia B. uniQure sought a stay of the impeachment action due to ongoing re-examination of the patent, but the Federal Court dismissed the stay motion, finding it not in the interests of justice. The court balanced the impact of re-examination, discovery needs, and prejudice, ultimately allowing the impeachment action to proceed without stay.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: uniQure, the Defendant, moves to stay the patent impeachment action due to ongoing re-examination of its Patent.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The Patent relates to a modified Factor IX protein used in gene therapy for hemophilia B, covering uniQure's HEMGENIX® product.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Pfizer seeks to impeach the Patent alleging anticipation, obviousness, lack of utility, overbreadth, unpatentable subject-matter, and misrepresentation of inventorship.

citations.why: Cited for section 53 on inventorship misrepresentation

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court finds it not in the interests of justice to grant the stay after considering context, length, purpose, impact, and prejudice.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The Patent's three independent claims require at least 70% sequence identity with specified FIX sequences, allowing up to 30% variability.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Impugned claims specify leucine or aspartic acid at position 338 and dosage range; leucine variant R338L is found in patients.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The SOC alleges anticipation by Stafford, obviousness, lack of demonstration for claim breadth, unpatentable subject-matter, and inventorship misrepresentation.
idea_list: lack of demonstration for claim breadth

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Pfizer intends to sell its gene therapy product in Canada, with Phase 3 trials done but no regulatory submission yet.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: uniQure requested re-examination of the Patent on October 21, 2022, citing new prior art from foreign proceedings involving Pfizer.

citations.why: Cited for re-examination request procedure

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The Re-examination Board accepted a substantial new question of patentability for independent claims, especially utility, but not for dependent claims.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: uniQure filed Proposed Claims narrowing scope, removing 70% identity and dosage limits, focusing on patient-found sequence.

citations.why: Cited for filing reply with proposed amendments

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The Board has until April 14, 2024 to decide re-examination, with possible outcomes including maintaining, cancelling, or adopting amended claims.

citations.why: Cited for possible re-examination outcomes

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: uniQure undertakes not to defend extant claims if the Board accepts any amendments.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The Action is early; discovery not started; Pfizer proposed discovery completion by April 2024; trial not before 2025.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Mylan explains the Court's stay discretion is like scheduling, distinct from enjoining other bodies, with public interest in fair, timely proceedings.

citations.cite: Mylan Pharmaceuticals ULC v AstraZeneca Canada Inc, 2011 FCA 312
citations.why: Explains Court's discretion to stay its own proceeding

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Stay discretion depends on factual context, guided by just, expeditious, least expensive determination and prejudice considerations.

citations.why: Factual context for stay discretion

citations.cite: ArcelorMittal Exploitation minière Canada SENC v Canada (Attorney General), 2021 FC 998 at para 19
citations.why: Factual context for stay discretion

citations.cite: Windsor (City) v Canadian Transit Co, 2016 SCC 54 at para 124
citations.why: Guidance on just, expeditious, least expensive determination and prejudice

citations.cite: Coote v Lawyers’ Professional Indemnity Company, 2013 FCA 143 at paras 12-13
citations.why: Guidance on stay discretion factors

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Balancing timely proceedings with whether another body's decision will materially impact litigation is relevant to stay discretion.

citations.cite: Clayton v Canada (Attorney General), 2018 FCA 1 at para 28
citations.why: Balancing expeditiousness and fairness

citations.cite: Iris Technologies v Canada (Revenue Agency), 2023 FC 188 at paras 34-35
citations.why: Prematurity if another body's decision materially impacts litigation

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: uniQure argues stay is needed because claim scope is undefined and re-examination may narrow issues, affecting discovery and expert reports.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Pfizer argues stay should be rare, re-examination impact is speculative, undertaking is conditional, and uniQure hasn't proven prejudice.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court finds stay will not sufficiently narrow issues or prejudice uniQure to justify granting it in the interests of justice.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court distinguishes Iristel, where stay was granted due to exclusive jurisdiction over a material issue, unlike here.

citations.why: Distinguishes Iristel stay precedent as not analogous

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Amendments by the Board won't dispose of the Action as key allegations remain, so re-examination won't resolve the litigation.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Board may not accept uniQure's amendments removing dosage limits; Board restricts claim scope broadening under Patent Act.

citations.why: Limits on claim amendments not broadening monopoly

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Dependent claims' fate is unclear; uniQure's conditional undertaking does not fully address this uncertainty.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: uniQure claims discovery would narrow without utility and claim breadth issues, but inventor conduct discovery remains necessary.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Sanofi confirms inventor's course of conduct is relevant to obviousness analysis.

citations.cite: Apotex Inc v Sanofi-Synthelabo Canada Inc, 2008 SCC 61
citations.why: Inventor's conduct relevant to obviousness

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Pfizer alleges it was obvious to try the R338L variant as a FIX replacement therapy by the relevant date.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: uniQure denies skilled persons would have been motivated or aware of the invention's unexpected benefits.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The inventor's conduct is in issue; no authority supports limiting discovery on it; uniQure's position lacks jurisprudence.

citations.why: No support for limiting discovery on inventor's conduct

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Iristel would not have sued without withheld tax refunds; claims depend on refund right, per Hester v Canada.

citations.cite: Hester v Canada, [2007] GSTC 172 (Ont. Sup. Ct.) at paras 53 and 54
citations.why: Shows claim foundation on tax refund right
Confirms dismissal of leave in Hester

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court finds it premature to hear the Claim while the Tax Court Appeals on Assessments' validity and tax refunds remain unresolved.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court notes the Tax Court Appeals outcome will affect the Claim's merits, supporting a stay request based on judicial economy.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court explains that if the Tax Court finds Assessments valid, Iristel's damage claim would likely fail, as Iristel conceded.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: If Iristel wins the Tax Court Appeals, it would simplify the current action by removing the need to litigate Assessments' lawfulness.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court states uniQure chose its litigation strategy and cannot claim prejudice from its own delay or avoid discovery by admissions.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court rejects uniQure's concern that Pfizer would use summary trial tactics, accepting Pfizer's counsel's assurance to seek an early trial date instead.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court is not persuaded uniQure will be unfairly prejudiced by parallel proceedings, as key patentability issues remain and procedural tools exist.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court notes the Board can take up to 12 months for re-examination, which is not short, and the re-examination impact should be significant to justify delay.

citations.why: Re-examination impact must be significant to justify delay

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court observes the Patent Act allows re-examination and impeachment to proceed in parallel, as it does not bar impeachment during re-examination.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court rejects uniQure's argument of no urgency, noting Pfizer's commercial interest and the duty to proceed expeditiously per Clayton.

citations.why: Duty to proceed expeditiously and fairly in litigation

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Balancing responsibilities and uncertain re-examination impact, the court finds no reason to grant a stay.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court concludes that granting a stay would not serve justice and dismisses the motion.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The parties agree on $5,000 costs but disagree on payment timing; uniQure wants costs in the cause, Pfizer wants immediate payment.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court states rule 401(2) allows immediate costs if a motion was improperly brought or opposed, but this motion does not qualify.

citations.cite: rule 401(2) of the Federal Courts Rules
citations.why: Court's power to order immediate costs

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court exercises discretion to award $5,000 costs to Pfizer in any event of the cause.

citations.why: Factors guiding court's discretion on costs

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court explains that quick, easy invention by the inventor may support obviousness unless their knowledge exceeds that of a skilled person.
